page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.large is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading. The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.se1.large operates in the lower performance tiers. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is measured at 1098.69, while multi-core performance reaches 1458.9. Memory bandwidth tests show 81.55 GB/sec for cached small blocks, dropping to 10.74 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 9.67 GB/sec for writes. Geekbench scores are also modest, with a single-core score of 920.0 and a multi-core score of 1092.0. Database operations, such as Redis SET, achieve 1.43 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is recorded at 1.28 GB/sec.

This instance offers a qualitative cost-efficient entry point for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high compute power. The primary tradeoff is the low processing throughput and memory bandwidth relative to the allocated RAM capacity. Consequently, the ecs.se1.large is best suited for lightweight database caching, small-scale Redis deployments, basic web serving, and memory-optimized development or testing environments where compute performance is not a critical constraint.
